resources.string: While paused, everything is silenced, including alarms (Alarm Bridge) and DND sync
Keep alarm forwarding, Do Not Disturb sync and sound-profile sync working while paused
While paused, ordinary notifications stay silent, but alarm forwarding to the watch, Do Not Disturb sync and sound-profile sync keep working
Light up the watch screen for new notifications. This controls the screen only — sound and vibration on the watch are set up separately and keep working even with the screen off.
Do not wake while phone is unlocked
Do not wake or play sound on the watch while the phone is in use

Silent (low-importance, no-sound) notifications already arrive on the phone without a sound or vibration of their own — screen and vibration on the watch are configured separately for them, apart from ordinary notifications.
Usually pointless: a silent notification reaches the watch collapsed, showing only the watch face — lighting the screen just wastes battery.
Useful: a silent notification arrives on the watch completely unnoticed — no sound and no vibration. This vibration is the only way to feel it.

For silent notifications to reach the watch at all, OHealth needs "Do not sync notifications without a sound" turned off (OHealth → Device → Notifications). Without that, the OnePlus stock sync filters such notifications out before they ever reach the watch, and Wake My Watch can\'t do anything about it.
Show notifications the watch never gets

Some notifications never reach the watch at all — for example private messages sent as a lone group summary with nothing nested inside, which the stock sync loses in transit. The watch buzzes with nothing to open. This shows those, and only those, on the watch itself. Anything the watch already receives is left alone, so nothing is duplicated. New, off by default — turn it on and see if it helps.
Sync the sound profile between phone and watch

Change the sound mode on the phone and the watch follows. Off by default.

"Sound" and "vibrate" carry straight over. When the phone goes "silent" the watch goes quiet through Do Not Disturb (on OnePlus phones via Do Not Disturb sync, on other phones through Wake My Watch with ADB access — see Permissions and background).

The watch's sleep mode is never carried to the phone: the phone stays as you left it at night.
Also switch the mode from the watch

Off by default: the watch only follows the phone. Turn on to also change the phone\'s sound mode by changing it on the watch. \"Silent\" from the watch is still ignored — that comes from its sleep mode, not from you, and it would otherwise drop the phone into Do Not Disturb at night on its own.

Inside a plan\'s quiet period the phone switches to \"vibrate\"; when no plan is active, to \"sound\". Plans may overlap. The schedule never touches \"silent\". If you change the profile by hand mid-period, the schedule leaves it alone until the next start/end time. The watch follows the phone automatically when sound profile sync is on.

Days apply to the start of the quiet period. A 23:00–07:00 plan with Friday ticked runs from Friday evening into Saturday morning, even though Saturday isn\'t ticked. It won\'t start across midnight from a day that isn\'t ticked.
Do not play an additional notification sound

On OnePlus Watch 4 the built-in notification sound gets cut off — instead of the full sound you hear a short, clipped version. This experimental setting helps the watch play it correctly. It does not replace the system sound and does not add its own — it only fixes the cut-off.
Do not wake the screen when the watch is off-wrist
Do not play an additional sound when the watch is off-wrist
These options are applied only when the watch supports the low-latency off-body sensor.
Also require the watch screen to be locked

Experimental. The off-body sensor can be wrong right after the watch-side process restarts, briefly reporting a worn watch as off-wrist. When on, off-wrist only counts if the sensor says so AND the watch screen is locked — Wear OS locks the watch the moment it actually leaves the wrist, so an unlocked watch is on the wrist for certain. If the watch has no screen lock set up, behavior is unchanged.

Do not wake the screen off-wrist

Sync Do Not Disturb between phone and watch
Send manual Do Not Disturb changes between the phone and watch. This feature is disabled on OnePlus/Oppo/Realme phones to avoid conflicts with the built-in Do Not Disturb sync on the watch.
All eligible notifications can wake the watch.
Forward phone alarms to the watch (Alarm Bridge)

Reliable synchronization is guaranteed only for alarms created in Google Clock. Manufacturer and third-party alarm apps may work partially or not at all because of Android restrictions. On OnePlus phones this can also duplicate OHealth alarm synchronization.\n\nThe alarm sound on the watch always plays, even with the screen off — you won\'t oversleep. The screen with control buttons appears immediately and restores itself after a short screen-off (3–5 sec). If the watch screen was off for longer (5+ sec), to bring the buttons back tap the \"Wake My Watch\" notification on the watch → \"Open on watch\", or control the alarm from the phone.

Do Not Disturb access on the watch

Without this access Wake My Watch can\'t carry Do Not Disturb from the phone to the watch (on OnePlus phones OHealth does this without ADB — the access is for other phones). Granted over ADB only — see the guide below.

Without this access Wake My Watch can\'t carry Do Not Disturb from the phone to the watch (on OnePlus phones OHealth does it — the access is for other phones). It\'s also what lets the phone\'s \"Silent\" mode switch on Do Not Disturb for the watch. Granted over ADB only — see the guide below.
Phone permissions for DND Sync are missing. Check the items below.
Some Android restrictions cannot be handled through a normal permission prompt. If wake, reminders or DND are unstable, check the items below.

1. Open Wake My Watch App info.
2. Enable notifications.
3. In battery settings choose Unrestricted, Do not optimize, or a similar option.
4. If the three-dot menu contains Allow restricted settings, enable it and confirm with password or fingerprint.
5. If the system kills apps from memory, lock Wake My Watch in the recent apps screen.
Settings → Apps → Wake My Watch → Battery → choose Unrestricted. Then check Notifications and Special app access → Do Not Disturb access.

Settings → Apps → Wake My Watch → Battery → choose Unrestricted. Also check Settings → Battery → Background usage limits and make sure Wake My Watch is not in Sleeping or Deep sleeping apps. You can also lock the app from the recent apps menu.
Settings → Apps → Wake My Watch → Battery saver → choose No restrictions. Enable Autostart if available. In recent apps, hold the Wake My Watch card and tap the lock if available.
Settings → Apps → Wake My Watch → Battery → allow background work. In app launch settings, disable automatic management for Wake My Watch and allow auto-launch, secondary launch and background run.

On newer OnePlus watches (Watch 4), use the watch\'s own DND/Bedtime sync setting. Older watches (Watch 2/2R/3) may not have native sync — use Wake My Watch\'s software DND sync instead. For other Wake My Watch features, open App info → Battery and choose an unrestricted mode if available. You can also lock the app in recent apps if the system removes it from memory.

Do Not Disturb sync on some Wear OS watches may require ADB setup. Open the separate “ADB for watch Do Not Disturb” guide: it shows the commands Wake My Watch needs, the adb pairing steps, and watch status verification. One more advanced system permission is not used by Wake My Watch yet and is only reserved for future sleep-mode sync.

ADB rights guide for DND sync with a non-OnePlus phone

On some Wear OS firmware versions, system screens do not show Wake My Watch or do not let the user grant Do Not Disturb access manually. For OnePlus Watch 2R, the reliable confirmed method is to grant two watch accesses through ADB.

On the watch, open Settings → Other → About watch → More version information, tap the build number repeatedly, then open Settings → Other → Developer options, enable Wi-Fi debugging and tap Connect new device.
2. Connect the watch from a PC
In platform-tools, run adb pair WATCH_IP:PAIR_PORT PAIR_CODE, then adb connect WATCH_IP:CONNECT_PORT. If several devices are connected, add -s WATCH_IP:PORT before shell.
Return to Wake My Watch on the watch and tap Refresh status. Both accesses should be granted and the status should become DND Sync ready.
Turn off Wi-Fi debugging on the watch. Do not leave wireless debugging enabled permanently: it wastes battery and is a security risk.
